mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each proposed director, shareholder and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in country of origin / issuing passport authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization: Notarization -> Authentication by competent authority in country of origin (e.g., US Department of State or MOFA of origin state) -> Legalization by Samoan Diplomatic or Consular Mission. Samoa is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or licensed corporate services provider of the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via the same notarization-authentication-consular chain

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source of wealth / source of funds statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via the same notarization-authentication-consular chain

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs and commercial counterparties against PEP definitions in the AML/CFT Act 2017; mandatory negative-news and sanctions screening against OFAC SDN, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated List and Samoa domestic designations under the UN Act 2001; enhanced due diligence for PEPs, source-of-funds verification, and periodic re-screening aligned to the Low_Risk_Standard medical PPE trade profile; electronic screening via World-Check/Refinitiv or equivalent commercial database.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies Office - Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) One-Stop Shop Registry, Apia; online lodgement via the MCIL Companies Online System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or Samoan, using the Latin (Roman) alphabet only; Samoan diacritics are permissible; the name must end with 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Corp' or 'Incorporated' or an accepted Samoan equivalent; non-Latin script names, names identical or confusingly similar to an existing registration, and misleading names are rejected; for sterile nitrile glove production, name tokens implying clinical endorsement such as 'Sterile', 'Medical', 'Surgical' or 'Hospital' may trigger mandatory consultation with the Ministry of Health.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trustee, Trust, Insurance, Assurance, Reinsurance, Finance, Financial Services - prior Central Bank of Samoa licence or consent required
Government, Ministry, Royal, Commonwealth, State, Public, National - prior Cabinet or Ministerial consent required
Building Society, Cooperative, University, Institute, Chamber - reserved terms requiring sector-specific licensing
Limited, Ltd, Corp, Inc (suffix misuse) - rejected under the Companies Act 2006
'Samoa' or 'Samoan' where the company is not in fact Samoan-owned or controlled - Registrar discretion
Medical, Sterile, Surgical, Hospital - Ministry of Health pre-consultation recommended for ISIC 3250 sterile glove manufacturing scope
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of the rejection notice, the applicant may request written reasons from the Registrar of Companies, MCIL. A formal reconsideration application with supporting submissions may be lodged within 21 days of receiving the written reasons. If the Registrar confirms the refusal, the applicant may institute judicial review proceedings in the Supreme Court of Samoa within 30 days, or alternatively reserve an amended name for a fresh 30-day period. Administrative fees apply at each stage under the Companies (Fees) Regulations.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as a substitute for the statutory registered office. The International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at all times, normally at the premises of its licensed Registered Agent; a PO Box, virtual address or purely digital workspace does not satisfy section 36 of the Companies Act 2006. The physical high-speed dipping nitrile glove factory may be located entirely outside Samoa, and no local operational staff are required at the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate for the registered office: quantified at 5-8% per annum from the Registrar of Companies and the Samoa FIU, given the Low_Risk_Standard banking classification for medical PPE consumables; however, if subsequent medical-device import or wholesale licensing is sought for a Samoan distribution entity, Ministry of Health physical inspection likelihood rises to approximately 30% during initial product registration and licensing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), ss. 5–12 (incorporation and memorandum), ss. 33–34 (registered office and agent), ss. 55–68 (directors, officers and resolutions), ss. 72–75 (share capital); supplemented by Companies Act 2001.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 – Application for Incorporation of an International Company, together with the Company's Constitution (Memorandum and Articles of Association) and Declaration of Compliance
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for an International Company; issued share capital may be expressed in any currency and no escrow, capital deposit or bank certificate is required at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the subscriptions to the International Company's constitution are hereby accepted, and the allotment of 1,000 ordinary shares of US$1.00 each at par to the founding subscriber is approved, with the subscription moneys credited to paid-up capital; (2) the registered office be fixed at the address of the licensed registered agent stated in the Certificate of Incorporation, and the registered agent be authorized to maintain statutory records; (3) the first directors, secretary and regulatory compliance officer designated by the founding shareholder are appointed to hold office until the next annual general meeting; and (4) the chairman and secretary of this meeting are authorized to file all incorporation returns and to open bank accounts with financial institutions in Samoa.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry, MCIL, online name reservation window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed English company name with the reserved suffix 'International Company' and a short business purpose statement. Obtain the name reservation certificate, then draft the constitution and internal governance provisions for review by the founding shareholder and licensed registered agent.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and business purpose statement
Identification details of proposed directors and shareholders
Consent of the intended registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen name is marked unavailable, submit a secondary name reservation through the same portal; the Registry may offer a phonetic or suffix modification without new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of incorporation application and constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry, MCIL, incorporation filings section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 and execute the constitution before a Notary Public licensed in Samoa. Submit the signed set, together with declarations of compliance and registered agent consent, to the Samoa International Companies Registry by courier or the MCIL online case-management portal. The registered agent must countersign the application.
required_dossiers: Form 1 – Application for Incorporation of an International Company
Power of Attorney if documents are signed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond with an amended Form 1 or constitution within 14 days; discuss through the registered agent and obtain a clear certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of government fees and issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MCIL cashier and Samoa International Companies Registry fee processing unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Follow the Registry-generated fee note; remit the filing and stamp fees through the MCIL cashier or designated bank. The amount shown on the fee note must match the schedule. After confirmation, the Registry will issue the Certificate of Incorporation electronically.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the submitted constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If fee payment is flagged as short, settle the assessed top-up through the MCIL cashier; incorporation process resumes upon receipt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting, officer appointments and registered office confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent and Samoa International Companies Registry corporate records section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting by circulation to the initial directors. Execute the first board resolution, obtain signed consents from each officer, open the statutory registers, and issue share certificates. Deliver the registered office and agent confirmations to the Registry if requested.
required_dossiers: Consent letters from directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry challenges officer consent forms or agent appointment, file amended consents immediately; no remedial fee is triggered for clerical omissions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation industrial, environmental and fire-safety licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MCIL Business Licence Division; Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment; Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the business licence application and supporting documents to MCIL Business Licence Division, and coordinate environmental and fire-safety inspections with MNRE and Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority before factory commissioning.
required_dossiers: Site plan and building occupancy permit
Fire safety plan and building clearance
Wastewater treatment and emissions control description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a licence application is queried or refused, cure the technical deficiency by filing an amended application within 21 business days, or appeal to the Business Licences Authority or Planning Appeals Board as applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Business Licence Division; Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) for environmental permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence (Manufacturing – Medical Examination Gloves) issued under the Business Licences Act 1997; additional Waste Disposal Permit under MNRE regulations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Planning and Urban Management Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category A – Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report mandatory for chemical manufacturing, dipping line operation, effluent discharge and air emission sources.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with Water Resources Management Act 2008 and WHO guidance: effluent BOD ≤ 30 mg/L; COD ≤ 125 mg/L; TSS ≤ 50 mg/L; pH 6.5–8.5; VOC emissions from compounding and dipping lines capped at 20 mg/m³; hazardous waste handling and disposal subject to Samoa waste management regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority under the Fire and Emergency Services Act 2007; building inspection certificate confirming structural safety and permitted industrial load under the Planning and Urban Management Act; occupational health and safety registration and periodic inspection by the MCIL Labour and Employment Division.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (Matagaluega o Tupe Maua), Government of Samoa; official portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws. Administering the Income Tax Act 2015, the Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) Act 2008, the Customs Act, and the Tax Administration Act 2012.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Samoa International Company obtains its Tax Identification Number (TIN) through the following procedure: (1) incorporation by a licensed registered agent with the Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), under the International Companies Act 1987; (2) submission of Form TIN-01 (Taxpayer Registration) to the Ministry for Revenue, attaching the certificate of incorporation, registered agent certificate, proof of registered office in Apia, certified passport copies of directors/shareholders, and the company's constitutional documents; (3) issuance of a 9-digit TIN by the Ministry for Revenue within 3-5 business days; (4) where required, separate registration for VAGST (Form VR-1) if the company makes taxable supplies in Samoa exceeding the annual threshold, and obtaining a Customs importer/exporter code from Samoa Customs. The International Company is exempt from income tax on its offshore business and pays only the annual international company government fee to SIFA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not operate a check-the-box or OECD hybrid-mismatch election regime. The International Company automatically enjoys statutory tax exemption under section 196 of the International Companies Act 1987, covering income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, estate duty, gift duty, and withholding tax on distributions to non-residents. Available statutory elections include: (i) voluntary VAGST registration under the VAGST Act 2008 for exporters or persons carrying on taxable activities in Samoa below the WST 100,000 compulsory threshold; (ii) elective conversion or continuation of an International Company into a domestic limited company under the Companies Act 2001, thereby subjecting the entity to the territorial Income Tax Act 2015 and standard Samoan company taxation; (iii) election to file an economic substance declaration under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Amendment Act for relevant activities; and (iv) group registration for VAGST purposes where related companies carry on taxable activities in Samoa.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 (Samoa Tala) of taxable supplies per annum; compulsory registration applies to any person carrying on a taxable activity in Samoa whose annual turnover exceeds this threshold. Offshore-to-offshore business of an International Company is generally outside the VAGST net as non-Samoa supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa currently imposes no mandatory real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based clearance mandate. VAGST-registered suppliers must issue tax invoices within 28 days of supply and retain records for 7 years; electronic invoices are accepted. Customs export declarations must be lodged electronically via the ASYCUDA World single-window platform (Customs Export Entry / Single Administrative Document), and VAGST returns (Form VAGST-01) are e-filed through the Ministry for Revenue Tax Administration System portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods exported from Samoa by a VAGST-registered exporter are zero-rated under the VAGST Act 2008 where: (i) the goods physically depart Samoa within 28 days of supply; (ii) the exporter retains conclusive evidence of export in the form of a Customs export declaration and bill of lading or air waybill; (iii) the consideration is receivable in convertible foreign currency and is not diverted for domestic use; and (iv) the goods are not subsequently returned to Samoa or consumed locally. Offshore services supplied to non-residents for use wholly outside Samoa, including international trading, logistics coordination, and re-invoicing of nitrile glove consignments, are also zero-rated or outside the scope of VAGST, provided the services are not performed in Samoa for a Samoan resident. Input VAGST attributable to zero-rated export activities is creditable, and the excess is refundable by the Commissioner of Revenue, typically within 30 days of lodgment of the return, subject to satisfactory substantiation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document lodged electronically via ASYCUDA World)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Samoa
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 / bank credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Commercial invoice and VAGST tax invoice
Packing list and certificate of origin (where preferential tariff treatment is claimed)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to substantive audit by the Ministry for Revenue and Samoa Customs. Under the Tax Administration Act 2012, failure to substantiate zero-rated export treatment results in assessment of VAGST at the standard 15% rate plus shortfall penalties of 20% for lack of reasonable care, 75% for gross carelessness, or 150% for intentional evasion, together with late payment penalties of 1.5% per month compounded and statutory interest. Fraudulent export zero-rating, including circular container movements, false bills of lading, phantom shipments, or unrepatriated proceeds, constitutes a criminal offence punishable by a fine of up to WST 100,000 and/or imprisonment of up to 7 years, with retrospective clawback of input credits and assessed VAGST for periods of up to 7 years, and no time limit in the case of fraud. Additionally, the offending International Company may lose confidentiality protections under the International Companies Act 1987 and face SIFA administrative sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) acting as the Exchange Control Authority pursuant to the Exchange Control Act 1970, the Exchange Control Regulations 1974, and the Money Laundering and Prevention of Money Laundering Act 2007, as amended.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa operates a partially convertible currency regime for the Samoan Tala (WST). Current-account payments for genuine imports of raw materials and trade-related services are screened by authorized dealers and are generally permissible upon submission of supporting commercial documents and Exchange Control Form A. Capital-account inflows, such as equity injections and shareholder loans into a resident Samoan branch of an International Company, require prior CBS Exchange Control approval unless routed through a licensed External Account. Profit remittances and dividend distributions by a tax-exempt International Company (WS_IC) are treated as offshore transactions under the International Companies Act and are not subject to Samoan withholding tax, but the beneficial owners must still satisfy CRS/FATCA reporting, and the bank must verify that the funds have clear provenance. The Tala is not freely convertible offshore; there is no liquid offshore WST market, so all conversions for operational purposes must be executed through a CBS-authorized dealer at the daily indicative rate. In practice, international treasury efficiency is achieved by maintaining a foreign-currency External Account and by settling cross-border obligations in USD or CNY outside Samoa.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBS Exchange Control Rules, exporters of medical PPE, including sterile powder-free nitrile examination gloves under ISIC 3250, must repatriate the full foreign-currency invoice value to Samoa through an authorized dealer within 90 days from the bill of lading date unless a prior exemption authority to retain proceeds in an External Account has been granted by the CBS. Upon repatriation, unless the exporter holds a written foreign-currency retention facility approved by the dealer and the CBS, 100% of the surrendered proceeds must be converted into WST at the prevailing bank-buying rate. For shipments settled by documentary letters of credit routed through a Samoan clearing bank, the permitted settlement window is extended to 180 days to accommodate the LC maturity, but the conversion requirement remains mandatory at the point of liquidation. An exporter may apply for standing exemption to retain USD export receipts in a designated External Account for direct repayment of imported nitrile polymer, machinery installments, and foreign freight, subject to quarterly verification by the Exchange Control Division.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Samoa does not license electronic money institutions as authorized dealers under the Exchange Control Act. Offshore digital EMIs cannot lawfully perform WST conversion, export-proceeds surrender, or trade-facilitation clearing because they are not connected to the Central Bank of Samoa Settlement System (CBSS). An EMI can be used peripherally as a receivable-collection tool for e-commerce PPE sales outside Samoa, subject to the funds being swept directly to a CBS-licensed operational account and subject to enhanced due diligence by the Samoan clearing bank. The overall feasibility rating is Low to Medium only where the EMI has robust correspondent banking through ANZ or BSP and holds no WST liability in Samoa.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: As a strict compliance baseline, at least one authorized director of the WS_IC must attend a physical KYC interview at the bank’s Apia office or at a Samoa diplomatic post where the bank has established an overseas verification protocol. Remote account opening may be permitted only where the ultimate beneficial owner and the signing director successfully complete a video-conference AML interview, produce a notarized board resolution, and engage a Samoa-licensed registered agent to physically attest the Beneficial Ownership Return (Form 55). In practice, because ISIC 3250 involves medical-device trade, Samoan banks require the factory-operating principal or an appointed treasury officer to appear in person for final signing and to verify the operational reality of the manufacturing site through a site inspection or an independent CPA visit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner identified as a high-net-worth Chinese family-trust client with non-transparent layered corporate ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full deed of trust and registered trust particulars; complete chain of incorporation certificates from the International Companies Register; sworn source-of-wealth statement supported by audited financials, bank references from a recognized Asia-Pacific bank, and a global CRS/FATCA self-certification; board resolution confirming no nominee concealment; and a lease or property title evidencing the physical glove-manufacturing plant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-flow ambiguity for a tax-exempt International Company that manufactures and exports medical gloves, producing an inconsistent pattern between reported revenues and received EFTP/MT103 credits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISO 13485:2016 certification for sterile glove manufacturing; CE/FDA/MHLW product registration; signed purchase orders from downstream medical distributors; customs-validated bill of lading and commercial invoice; import purchase order for NBR nitrile latex; warehouse inventory records; Samoan income-tax or tax-exemption confirmation from the Ministry of Revenue; and a transaction-level reconciliation linking each remittance to a specific shipment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of high-risk clearing jurisdictions or sanctions-adjacent financial centers for raw-material sourcing and trade settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-specific compliance heat map showing no sanctioned parties; shipping documents routed through acceptable transshipment hubs; ownership-chain certification from suppliers; United Nations and OFAC screening certificates; bank account confirmation from an authorized dealer in the source jurisdiction; and a letter from the Samoa International Finance Authority confirming the WS_IC’s valid registered status and good standing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward equity contributions and shareholder loans for the WS_IC must be transmitted via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 to the bank’s Samoan clearing code, quoting purpose code P1101 (Investment Capital under International Companies Act) and supported by a board resolution and share-allotment form. Where the investing entity is a Samoan resident or where the influx will be converted into WST to pay local wages, a prior Exchange Control Application Form (EC-A) must be approved by CBS within 5 business days. For investments above WST 100,000, the receiving bank must issue a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate or Capital Import Certificate to the CBS prior to applying funds to the WS_IC’s Capital Escrow Account. If the capital is held in USD for onward trade payments, it will remain in a Designated External Account; conversion to WST for local disbursement will be executed only against ECB-confirmed invoices.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for raw-material imports and freight will be cleared through the Samoan banking system using SWIFT MT103/MT103+ for TT open-account transactions, commercial standby and sight letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT701) for large polymer shipments, and documentary collections under URC 522 for mid-sized distributor deliveries. All payments exceeding USD 50,000 must be supported by a completed Exchange Control Form B, the underlying purchase order, a customs-supplier invoice, and a copy of the import license for nitrile polymer. WST-leg settlement occurs on the Central Bank of Samoa Settlement System (CBSS) via real-time gross settlement windows, while USD and CNY leg settlements are cleared through ANZ’s Sydney branch and BSP’s Port Moresby/Suva correspondent network.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts for USD/WST with an authorized dealer bank, tenor up to 12 months.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/WST and CNY/WST) where the underlying exposure is an approved external foreign-currency loan.
Plain-vanilla FX options (European exercise) purchased from an ANZ/BSP authorized dealer for hedging PPE export receivables.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and annual license fee payment (International Companies Act 1987, s.123)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission attracts a 10% penalty on the unpaid annual fee; failure to file within 6 months of the anniversary may trigger Registrar-initiated administrative strike-off and subsequent dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, SIFA (Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2017)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the Annual Return, within 30 days post-anniversary; any UBO change must be reflected in the register within 14 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Conviction-based monetary penalties under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2017; sustained non-compliance is treated as a breach of the International Companies Act and may support administrative strike-off by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Maintenance of current registered office and licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SIFA-licensed registered agent filing on behalf of the Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous requirement from incorporation; agent resignation must be remedied by new agent appointment within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of a licensed agent leaves the company without a statutory representative; failure to appoint a replacement within 30 days empowers the Registrar to strike the company off the register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Samoa International Company is unconditionally exempt from independent audit unless it constitutes a 'large international company' — defined as an entity whose shares are listed on a recognized stock exchange, which has more than 50 members, or which has made a public offer of its shares. This private, closely-held sterile glove manufacturing vehicle falls below those thresholds and is not audit-mandated.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) where an audit is statutorily triggered or voluntarily appointed; in all other cases, internal books and records must nevertheless reflect complete and accurate accounting on a consistent basis

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a Register of Beneficial Owners under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2017. Each member or transferee is obliged to notify the company of any change in beneficial ownership within 14 days; the company must update the register within a further 14 days, and the Annual Return must confirm that the register is accurate and complete as at the incorporation anniversary date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (records of directors' and members' meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Audit-exempt for standard private International Company; voluntary certified audit typically USD 2,000 – USD 5,000 per engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (resident companies); 0% for the International Company (non-resident, tax-exempt)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Samoa International Company is wholly exempt from income tax, dividend/interest/royalty withholding tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty and estate duty under s.198 of the International Companies Act 1987, provided it does not carry on business in Samoa and derives no Samoan-source income. For resident corporates, no general manufacturing holiday applies; capital allowances on plant and machinery (including dipping lines) are available under the Income Tax Act 1974 (as amended).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (Form AR-IC) filed electronically through the licensed Samoa registered agent with the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL); no income tax return is required for the tax-exempt IC.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 1 calendar month after each anniversary of incorporation; the registered agent lodges the return online and settles the annual government fee concurrently.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full registered name of the International Company
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the Certificate of Incorporation exactly.
Format WS-IC-XXXX; referenced in all banking, LC and TT documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical address of the registered office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provided by the licensed registered agent; a P.O. Box is not acceptable.
Agent must be retained at all times; agent resignation triggers strike-off risk within 90 days if not replaced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, nationalities and addresses of all directors
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors are permitted; at least one natural person is recommended for banking KYC purposes.
Bearer shares are prohibited since the 2008 amendment; the register of members must be kept at the registered office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized share capital and issued shares
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No minimum capital requirement; standard authorized capital is USD 1,000,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of no Samoan resident business, no Samoan real property and no regulated activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Critical: carrying on business within Samoa voids the statutory tax exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Government fee scale based on authorized capital
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Late payment accrues penalties and triggers strike-off risk.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-payment of the annual fee: MCIL imposes escalating default penalties (typically WST 50-500 plus per-month surcharges); persistent default leads to Gazette strike-off, deregistration and restoration costs; the registered agent is contractually liable for loss of good standing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Resident Company Income Tax Return (Form CIT-1) lodged with the Samoa Ministry for Revenue e-Services portal (MOR-TAS) - included only as the non-resident benchmark; the International Company does not complete this form.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the company's balance date (e.g., 30 June for a 31 December year-end); instalment payment obligations apply to large taxpayers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Turnover from all Samoan and foreign sources
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: IC non-resident income is outside the statutory gross income definition.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt categories including the IC exemption
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An IC would record 100% exempt income; exemption attaches by status and is not elective.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses incurred in deriving assessable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable for the IC; no deduction claim is necessary.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: penalty of up to 25% of outstanding tax plus monthly default interest at 10% per annum; evasion assessments carry 100-200% shortfall penalties and criminal prosecution with fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for the International Company: dividends paid by an IC to non-resident shareholders are statutorily exempt from Samoan withholding tax. Resident-company dividends paid to non-residents attract 15% WHT under the Income Tax Act 1974 (as amended).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not required for the IC because the domestic exemption removes the charge before treaty relief is considered. Where a resident company seeks treaty relief (Samoa's in-force DTA network is minimal; the country relies primarily on Tax Information Exchange Agreements), the non-resident recipient must lodge a Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by its home tax authority together with Form WHT-1 with the Samoa Ministry for Revenue; the payer must retain the TRC for 7 years, and reduced rates apply only where a DTA is in force.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: IC: interest paid to non-resident lenders 0% and royalties on the glove trademark and process IP 0%, both exempt from Samoan WHT. Resident-paying benchmarks: non-resident interest 15%, non-resident royalties 15%, subject to limited treaty reductions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa applies the OECD arm's length standard to resident taxpayers under the Tax Administration Act 2015. The tax-exempt IC is outside the Samoan TP net, but the contract-manufacturing affiliate in the production jurisdiction must hold contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation where related-party turnover exceeds the local threshold (commonly the lesser of WST 5,000,000 aggregate related-party turnover or WST 1,000,000 intra-group transactions, aligned with OECD TP documentation practice).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa has not enacted BVI/Cayman-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, OECD Global Forum membership and the 2008 International Companies Amendment Act impose substantive elements: licensed registered agent, registered office in Samoa, prohibition of bearer shares, and retention of accounting records at the registered office. For the nitrile-glove trade flow, the IC must evidence board decisions, contract negotiation, invoicing and cash settlement outside Samoa; a purely passive letterbox IC risks recharacterization as a sham in the counterparty jurisdiction and exclusion from banking and payment-rail facilities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Declaration (Samoa domestic law)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing false annual returns, omitting revenue or abusing the IC exemption by transacting with Samoa residents or deriving Samoan-source income while claiming the s.198 exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Shortfall penalties of 100-200% of tax evaded; monetary fines of up to WST 500,000 against the company; criminal conviction with imprisonment of up to 5 years; deregistration of the IC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners are jointly and severally liable for the tax shortfall where funds were distributed as dividends before settlement; travel restrictions and disqualification orders may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Samoa IC as a paper entity with no real commercial substance, circular invoices or back-to-back contracts designed only to divert margin from the true manufacturing and distribution activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the arrangement; denial of the exemption and withholding relief; imposition of Samoan corporate tax at 27% plus penalties if Samoan-source income is found; strike-off by the Registrar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Judicial lifting of the corporate veil: directors ordered to disgorge diverted profits; personal liability for unpaid taxes; arrest warrants or travel bans pending foreign investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using trade mis-invoicing, phantom LC draws or unexplained TT wire surges for the glove trade; knowingly moving proceeds for sanctioned persons or terrorist financing; failure of the registered agent to identify beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Company fines up to WST 2,000,000; confiscation of proceeds; revocation of the registered agent's license; freezing of bank accounts; criminal prosecution with imprisonment up to 14 years for responsible officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability for officers who knowingly participate in laundering; asset forfeiture, worldwide travel bans and extradition exposure under mutual legal assistance treaties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Regulatory Non-Compliance with the International Companies Act 1987
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the annual return, non-payment of the annual government fee, failure to keep accounting records at the registered office, or reissue of bearer-style share warrants.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late penalty charges; Gazette strike-off and deregistration; restoration fees of WST 500 plus all arrears; director disqualification in egregious cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors remain personally liable for company debts contracted after the strike-off point; management of a struck-off IC is an offense punishable by fine and imprisonment; travel bans may assist creditor recovery.
